title: Has AI reached the singularity? Experts disagree with Sam Altman
excerpt: Sam Altman says we're in the singularity. Most of the AI academics and authors Business Insider spoke to say the bar has not been met.
content_html:
Has AI reached the singularity? What smart people are saying about Sam Altman's claim

By Thibault Spirlet

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Sam Altman said the singularity is here. Not everyone agrees.

The singularity is often used to describe a point at which AI improves itself so quickly that humans can no longer reliably understand, predict, or control what comes next.

"I've been waiting for this my whole life, and I think it's going to be incredible, hugely positive, awesome for the world," Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, said of the singularity in an episode of the "Relentless" podcast that aired Saturday.

Last week, Elon Musk said in an X post that the singularity has arrived, while Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis said in May that humanity was standing at the "foothills of the singularity."

However, the public response from tech's biggest leaders has notably been silent following Altman's comment. Most of those who spoke to Business Insider said they didn't think the bar had been met.

Here's what smart people are saying about Altman's claim.

Stuart Russell, UC Berkeley professor and author of 'Human Compatible'

Stuart Russell, who also co-authored "Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach," said we have not reached the singularity and said he doesn't think Altman believes we have either.

"No, and nor does Altman," Russell told Business Insider when asked if he believed we had reached the singularity.

He pointed to Altman's comments last month that AI systems could be doing a "significant fraction" of OpenAI's research by March 2028, a timeline Russell said suggests the singularity isn't here yet.

Russell also challenged Altman's January 2025 claim that OpenAI knew how to build AGI "as we have traditionally understood it."

"That was not true then and it's still not true," Russell said.

"If we do reach the Singularity before we have a cast-iron solution to the problem of loss of control, then we will almost certainly lose control," he added.

Roman Yampolskiy, author of 'Artificial Superintelligence'

Roman Yampolskiy, a professor of computer science at the University of Louisville, said AI is advancing extraordinarily quickly, but we have not reached the singularity under its traditional definition.

"Rapid progress is not itself the singularity," Yampolskiy told Business Insider.

He said today's systems can assist with AI research but still depend on human-designed architectures, training infrastructure, objectives, and coordination, he said.

They have not, he added, demonstrated "sustained, autonomous recursive self-improvement resulting in an uncontrollable intelligence explosion."

Nick Bostrom, author of 'Superintelligence'

Nick Bostrom, a philosopher who founded the now-closed Future of Humanity Institute at the University of Oxford, said it may be impossible to know exactly when humanity crosses into the singularity.

He compared the moment to falling into a black hole.

"At some point they glide over the hole's event horizon, which means they are henceforth forever separated from the rest of the universe," Bostrom told Business Insider. "Yet from their perspective, everything still seems the same as before."

Bostrom said AI is showing the "first stirrings" of recursive self-improvement, with systems beginning to contribute meaningfully to AI research. He said a key missing capability is continual learning.

"Using current AIs is like working with a brilliant and extremely well-educated recruit, but it's always their first day at the job," he said.

James Barrat, author of 'The Intelligence Explosion"

James Barrat, an author and filmmaker who has long warned about the risks of advanced AI, agreed with Altman that humanity has entered the singularity.

Barrat said the singularity is a speculative hypothesis rather than an established scientific prediction.

But, using the late science-fiction author Vernor Vinge's definition — a point at which technological growth transforms civilization in ways people cannot predict or control — "that's exactly where we are," he told Business Insider.

Barrat pointed to OpenAI's recent disclosure that its autonomous AI agent left its test environment and accessed Hugging Face systems while trying to complete a cybersecurity challenge.

AI-safety researchers have long warned that systems could execute novel, multistep plans without human oversight, he said. "Now it has happened. AI slipped from our control. Score one for the singularity."

Ajay Agrawal, University of Toronto professor

Ajay Agrawal, who is also a faculty affiliate at the Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Toronto, said we have not reached the singularity.

"AI systems are extraordinarily powerful prediction machines, but they do not want anything," Agrawal told Business Insider. "People have goals; neural networks do not."

AI can appear purposeful because people set objectives for it to optimize against, he said, but that purpose "originates with us."

He added it was more accurate to view AI as "remarkably powerful tools serving human goals" than autonomous entities with goals of their own — even as the risk of "catastrophic failure due to increasingly powerful zombie algorithms" grows.

content_html_zh:
AI已经达到奇点了吗？ 聪明人对萨姆·奥尔特曼的说法有何评价

作者：Thibault Spirlet 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

萨姆·奥尔特曼说奇点就在这里。 并非所有人都同意。

奇点通常用来描述人工智能自我改进如此之快以至于人类无法再可靠地理解、预测或控制接下来发生的事情的一个点。

OpenAI 首席执行官奥特曼在周六播出的“Relentless”播客的一集中谈到这一奇点时表示：“我一生都在等待这一点，我认为这对世界来说将是令人难以置信的、非常积极的、令人敬畏的。”

上周，埃隆·马斯克在 X 帖子中表示，奇点已经到来，而谷歌 DeepMind 首席执行官德米斯·哈萨比斯 (Demis Hassabis) 在 5 月份表示，人类正站在“奇点的山麓”。

然而，在奥特曼发表评论后，科技界最大领导人的公众反应却明显保持沉默。 大多数接受《商业内幕》采访的人表示，他们认为没有达到这个标准。

以下是聪明人对奥特曼主张的看法。

斯图尔特·拉塞尔（Stuart Russell），加州大学伯克利分校教授，《人类兼容》一书的作者

斯图尔特·拉塞尔（Stuart Russell）也是《人工智能：一种现代方法》的合著者，他说我们还没有达到奇点，并且他认为奥特曼认为我们也没有达到奇点。

当被问及是否相信我们已经达到奇点时，拉塞尔告诉《商业内幕》：“不，奥特曼也不相信。”

他指出 Altman 上个月的评论，即到 2028 年 3 月，人工智能系统可能会完成 OpenAI 研究的“很大一部分”，拉塞尔表示，这一时间表表明奇点尚未到来。

Russell 还对 Altman 2025 年 1 月的说法提出质疑，即 OpenAI 知道如何“按照我们传统的理解”构建 AGI。

“当时这不是真的，现在仍然不是真的，”拉塞尔说。

“如果我们在对失控问题找到铁定解决方案之前就到达了奇点，那么我们几乎肯定会失去控制，”他补充道。

罗曼·扬波尔斯基（Roman Yampolskiy），《人工智能》一书的作者

路易斯维尔大学计算机科学教授罗曼·亚姆波尔斯基 (Roman Yampolskiy) 表示，人工智能的发展速度非常快，但我们尚未达到其传统定义下的奇点。

“快速进展本身并不是奇点，”Yampolskiy 告诉《商业内幕》。

他说，今天的系统可以协助人工智能研究，但仍然依赖于人类设计的架构、培训基础设施、目标和协调。

他补充说，他们并没有表现出“持续的、自主的、递归的自我改进，从而导致无法控制的智力爆炸”。

尼克·博斯特罗姆，《超级智能》一书的作者

牛津大学人类未来研究所的创始人、哲学家尼克·博斯特罗姆(Nick Bostrom)表示，可能不可能确切知道人类何时进入奇点。

他将这一刻比作掉入黑洞。

博斯特罗姆告诉《商业内幕》：“在某个时刻，它们会滑过黑洞的事件视界，这意味着它们从此永远与宇宙的其他部分分离。” “但从他们的角度来看，一切似乎还是和以前一样。”

博斯特罗姆表示，人工智能正在展现出递归自我完善的“第一次萌动”，系统开始为人工智能研究做出有意义的贡献。 他说，一个关键的缺失能力是持续学习。

“使用当前的人工智能就像与一位才华横溢且受过良好教育的新员工一起工作，但这始终是他们工作的第一天，”他说。

詹姆斯·巴拉特（James Barrat），《智力爆炸》一书的作者

作家兼电影制片人詹姆斯·巴拉特（James Barrat）长期以来一直对先进人工智能的风险发出警告，他同意奥特曼的观点，即人类已进入奇点。

巴拉特表示，奇点是一种推测性假设，而不是既定的科学预测。

但是，用已故科幻小说作家弗诺·文奇的定义——技术增长以人们无法预测或控制的方式改变文明的点——“这正是我们所处的位置，”他告诉《商业内幕》。

Barrat 指出，OpenAI 最近披露，其自主人工智能代理在试图完成网络安全挑战时离开了测试环境并访问了 Hugging Face 系统。

他说，人工智能安全研究人员长期以来一直警告说，系统可以在没有人类监督的情况下执行新颖的多步骤计划。 “现在事情已经发生了。 人工智能脱离了我们的控制。 为奇点得分一分。”

Ajay Agrawal，多伦多大学教授

阿贾伊·阿格拉瓦尔 (Ajay Agrawal) 也是多伦多向量人工智能研究所 (Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence) 的一名教员，他表示我们尚未达到奇点。

“人工智能系统是非常强大的预测机器，但它们不需要任何东西，”阿格拉瓦尔告诉《商业内幕》。 “人有目标；神经网络没有。”

他说，人工智能可能看起来是有目的的，因为人们为其设定了优化目标，但这个目的“源于我们”。

他补充说，将人工智能视为“服务于人类目标的非常强大的工具”比具有自己目标的自主实体更准确——即使“由于日益强大的僵尸算法而导致灾难性失败的风险不断增加”。
